audit.why: The prose addresses the owner in second person, so third-person pronouns refer to the enemy. These templates were authored for a male enemy and only the champion name was substituted, leaving the pronouns wrong. champ-data/champ-gender.js is the authority.

edits.before: Lux wins the early walk-up by simply out-ranging Alistar: her Q and E let her poke him and his ADC from a distance he can never close, and any step forward into W-Q range means eating a nuke. His mana pool can't sustain repeated failed engages, so he falls behind on health and pressure in the first two levels.
edits.after: Lux wins the early walk-up by simply out-ranging Alistar: her Q and E let her poke her and her ADC from a distance she can never close, and any step forward into W-Q range means eating a nuke. Her mana pool can't sustain repeated failed engages, so she falls behind on health and pressure in the first two levels.

edits.before: Through 3-6 Lux's Light Binding is the ideal deterrent to a telegraphed engage: she holds Q to root Alistar the moment he commits his W-Q, wasting his flash, and her constant poke keeps him too low to force. He has no mobility to dodge her skillshots reliably, so he's stuck reacting to her zone control.
edits.after: Through 3-6 Lux's Light Binding is the ideal deterrent to a telegraphed engage: she holds Q to root Alistar the moment she commits her W-Q, wasting her flash, and her constant poke keeps her too low to force. edits.before: In 2-item teamfights Alistar can flank to threaten Lux, but her Q root and Finales Funkeln burst punish his approach, and because he deals no damage his landed knockup rarely converts into a kill. Lux out-ranges and out-damages the duel at every stage, so she stays ahead from lane through late-game fights.
